note: A steward-held [[errata.column]] without a curated type is typed from SWECOV storage under the register's steward table prefixes, widened over every matching table; a curated type wins; storage that cannot widen leaves it untyped and names the evidence; a column the source documents blocks the entry. Expected literals: c-stew decimal and the provenance 'CIS2004=smallint, CIS2012=float', its is_identifier 1 and is_sensitive 0, c-cur integer over CIS2016 varchar, c-mix null with 'CIS2004=date, CIS2012=int' in the unknown_data_type detail, and c-nopfx null (storage only under a non-matching prefix; old: prefixes ('NONE',) -> data_type None), all from test_steward_storage_type_and_flags_preserve_curated_identifier. Each entry names versions = ["2020"] while the register also delivers 2018 and 2022 (EDITION, var 99), so each forms exactly one 2020 state (valid_to 2020-12-31): test_column_declaration_preserves_only_supplied_flags_and_periods[FIX-versions1] binds its one addition to the 2020 edition (addition.edition_key == binding.key) beside a later delivered edition that gains none (len(additions) == 1). The fifth entry reproduces that test's documented column in both arms: it declares BLK for 2020, and the source documents the column by name only as Blk (var 31) in 2022, another spelling in another edition (var 31's 2020 row has a blank column), as the old test's record documents 'missing' in 2021 against a 'MISSING' declaration for 2020. The entry is refused as column_now_documented (blocked.blockers == ('column_now_documented',)), in the '<entry locator>: <blockers>' format the compile reports, and forms no c-documented state (`not any(item.occurrence_key for item in stale.occurrences)`). The old test also replays the compiled case against a source that documents the column and expects the apply-time column-absent guard to mark it stale; in a build the compile reads the same variant records first (curation_compile.py builds each variant's records from the register slice; scb_errata.py convert_column_entry checks `context.by_column` before it emits the guard), so the refusal above is the boundary outcome. Prose kept on purpose: the stale row's detail is the only boundary signal of its blocker code, and c-mix's issue detail is the old test's own assertion that the diagnostic names the storage evidence (its refs cite only the Registerinformation row). The applied c-stew and c-cur entries raise no issue, as the replaced test_column_declaration_preserves_only_supplied_flags_and_periods asserts for an applied declaration (`result.diagnostics == ()`).
fails_if: `scb_errata.convert_column_entry` stops inferring a steward-held column's type from storage, lets storage override a curated `data_type`, drops a curated `is_identifier`, adds a declared column to editions its `versions` do not name, or stops refusing a column the source documents (`column_now_documented`), including one documented under another spelling or only in another edition (for example by looking up `entry.column` unfolded, or only in the named editions)
